minutes.headline: Agricultural Commission approved the 2021 farmers market vendor application, with lower fees and a later start, by roll call.
minutes.summary: The commission met remotely and spent most of the meeting on the 2021 farmers market vendor application. The market managers presented changes: a June start, shorter Sunday hours, no market on the fourth, and lower vendor fees. The application was approved by roll call and the meeting adjourned at 7:32.

public_comment.topic: Update on Cherry Hill Farm: 18 cows in the barn, four milking, more calving soon, and the farmer recovering from shoulder surgery.
Stephanie asked whether the commission's letter to animal control about farm inspections had received a reply; the chair said it had not yet been sent.
Stephanie described a micro-farm boarding horses without a boarding permit, with manure near wetlands, and asked where to direct neighbors; the chair asked her to email him.

votes.motion: Approve the market regulations and vendor application for the 2021 season, by roll call.

budget_items.what_was_said: Entertainers will be invited but not reimbursed from the agricultural fund, which is one reason for the lower fee. The pandemic's effect on vendors was another.

decisions.decision: The chair asked Stephanie to email him about the horse boarding concern, and said he would send the animal control letter.
The market manager will contact the board of health and returning and new vendors now that the application is approved.
No new signs this year; existing signs will be reused and social media outreach used instead.
The next meeting is set for April 15 at seven o'clock.

what_happened.line: The Agricultural Commission approved the 2021 farmers market regulations and vendor application by roll call, unanimously.
The application lowers the full-season vendor fee and cuts the daily rate with a cap.
Entertainers will be invited but not reimbursed from the agricultural fund, which was given as one reason for the lower fee.
No new market signs this year; existing signs will be reused and social media used instead.
In public comment, a resident raised a horse boarding concern near wetlands; the chair asked her to email him and said he would send the animal control letter.

why_it_matters: Vendors face lower fees for the 2021 market season, which may make it cheaper for small farms and food sellers to take part.
The market is run partly from the agricultural fund, so not reimbursing entertainers is a spending choice that keeps fee revenue and costs in balance.
